chunks: Certainly, your assignment is not a morsel for you,
but it is a trust round your neck,
and you have been charged with the protection (of the people) on behalf of your superiors.
It is not for you to be oppressive towards the ruled,
nor to risk yourself save on strong grounds.
You have in your hands the funds which are the property of Allāh, to Whom belongs Might and Majesty,
and you hold its charge till you pass it on to me.
Probably, I will not be one of the bad rulers for you,
and that is an end to the matter.
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical duties of a governor according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) characterizes governance as a divine amanah (trust) where the ruler acts as a steward of God’s wealth, emphasizing that public funds are held in custody until final accountability. This letter underscores the ethical imperative of just conduct and careful management of resources, warning the governor that he is accountable to the Imam and, ultimately, to God for his stewardship.
